# temps_network_policy_rule (Resource)

Allows or denies traffic between a workload (a project, environment or service) and a peer at the network layer of the cluster.

Import with `<id>`.

Required API key permissions: `settings:read`, `system:admin`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Workloads of service 12 may not send mail directly.
resource "temps_network_policy_rule" "no_smtp" {
  subject_kind = "service"
  subject_id   = 12
  direction    = "egress"
  action       = "deny"
  peer_kind    = "cidr"
  peer_ref     = "0.0.0.0/0"
  protocol     = "tcp"
  port_start   = 25
  port_end     = 25
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `action` (String) What to do with matching traffic. One of `allow`, `deny`.
- `direction` (String) Traffic direction. One of `ingress`, `egress`.
- `peer_kind` (String) Kind of peer. One of `service`, `workload`, `cidr`, `host`.
- `peer_ref` (String) The peer: a CIDR, or an ID for other kinds.
- `subject_id` (Number) ID of that workload.
- `subject_kind` (String) Kind of workload the rule is about. One of `deployment`, `sandbox`, `service`, `function`, `job`.

### Optional

- `description` (String) Why the rule exists.
- `port_end` (Number) Last port of the range.
- `port_start` (Number) First port of the range.
- `protocol` (String) `tcp`, `udp` or `any`.

### Read-Only

- `enforceable` (Boolean) Whether the nodes can enforce the rule.
- `id` (String) Import ID, `<id>`.
- `origin` (String) Who created the rule.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <id>
terraform import temps_network_policy_rule.no_smtp 17
```
